deep.reconstruction:
Context (p.121). lambda(a) = log|a| + i*theta(a) is a fixed logarithm. Checking the p.121 formulas shows it behaves exactly like the principal branch on the relevant region (arg in (-pi,pi], with arg = pi on the negative reals). Hilbert writes '+pi' where '+i*pi' is meant. So e^{-s lambda(a)} = a^{-s} (principal). On p.121 he had the non-integral-weight Eisenstein-type series phi(z) = sum (mu z+nu)^{-s} and psi(z) = sum (mu z-nu)^{-s} over mu,nu >= 0, (mu,nu) != (0,0). He proved the exact branch identities:
(A) lambda(mu(-1/z)+nu) = lambda(nu z-mu) - lambda(z)
(B) lambda(mu(-1/z)-nu) = lambda(nu z+mu) - lambda(z) + i*pi
for mu,nu >= 0 and Im z > 0. This gave phi(-1/z) = e^{s lambda(z)} psi(z) and psi(-1/z) = e^{s(lambda(z)-i pi)} phi(z).

This page.

(1) Definition. For Im z > 0 and Im z' > 0:
f(z,z') = sum_{mu>=0, nu in Z, (mu,nu)!=(0,0)} exp(-s[lambda(mu z+nu) + lambda(mu z'-nu)]).
Up to branch bookkeeping this is sum [(mu z+nu)(mu z'-nu)]^{-s}. It is a two-variable, weight-(s,s) Eisenstein-type series. The two logarithms are taken separately, not as the log of the product. Convergence (my addition): |mu z+nu| >= c(|mu|+|nu|) and likewise for z', so the series converges absolutely for Re s > 1, uniformly on compacta.

(2) Translation: f(z+1, z'-1) = f(z,z'). [My step] mu(z+1)+nu = mu z+(nu+mu) and mu(z'-1)-nu = mu z'-(nu+mu). For each fixed mu the substitution nu -> nu-mu permutes Z. The arguments of lambda are literally the same numbers, so there is no branch issue.

(3) Inversion: f(-1/z,-1/z') = e^{s(lambda(z)+lambda(z')-i pi)} f(z,z'). [My verification, term by term, using (A),(B)]
- Case nu >= 0: apply (A) to the z-factor and (B) to the z'-factor. The sum of logs becomes lambda(mu'z+nu') + lambda(mu'z'-nu') - lambda(z) - lambda(z') + i pi, with (mu',nu') = (nu,-mu).
- Case nu = -n < 0: apply (B) to the z-factor and (A) to the z'-factor. This gives the same shape with (mu',nu') = (n,mu).
So each term picks up exactly the factor e^{s(lambda(z)+lambda(z')-i pi)}, with no stray e^{2 pi i k s}. This is the Hilbert-type modular relation for the diagonal action (z,z') -> (-1/z,-1/z') together with (z,z') -> (z+1,z'-1). It is the action of SL2(Z) on z and of its conjugate by diag(1,-1) on z'.

(4) Reparametrisation. Put z' = -z'' with Im z'' < 0, and define a logarithm on the lower half-plane by lambda~(w) := lambda(-w). This is what 'lambda(z'') = lambda(z')' means. Then mu z'-nu = -(mu z''+nu), and
g(z,z'') := f(z,-z'') = sum exp(-s[lambda(mu z+nu) + lambda~(mu z''+nu)]).
The relations become:
- g(z+1, z''+1) = g(z,z'');
- g(-1/z,-1/z'') = e^{s(lambda(z)+lambda~(z'')-i pi)} g(z,z'').
The factor is the illegible/struck symbol in the MS. Hilbert's line 'g(z+1,z''+1) = g(-1/z,-1/z'') = ...g(z,z'')' compresses two separate relations.

(5) Specialisation z = xi + i eta, z'' = conj(z) = xi - i eta. Then (mu z+nu)(mu z''+nu) = |mu z+nu|^2 = (mu xi+nu)^2 + mu^2 eta^2 =: Q(mu,nu). Q is a positive definite binary quadratic form of discriminant -4 eta^2.
[My check] arg lambda~(mu zbar+nu) = pi - arg(mu z+nu) in every case, so the phases add to exactly pi. Hence
g(z, zbar) = e^{-i pi s} sum_{half-lattice} Q(mu,nu)^{-s}.
This is Hilbert's 'sum 1/psi^s of Dirichlet, Kronecker, Weber' (continued on p.123). It is the Epstein/Dirichlet zeta function of the form; equivalently eta^{-s} times the real-analytic Eisenstein series E(z,s) = sum eta^s |mu z+nu|^{-2s}.

Purpose. To realise the classical, non-holomorphic zeta function of a binary quadratic form as the restriction to the anti-diagonal of a function holomorphic in two independent variables, with explicit modular functional equations. On p.123 he passes to u = z+z', v = zz': the binary quadratic x^2 - u xy + v y^2, with SL2 acting ternarily and preserving the conic u^2 - 4v = 0.
errors: Notation slip (here and on p.121): '+pi' / '-pi' in the exponents must be '+i*pi' / '-i*pi', since lambda(a) = l_r(a) + i*theta. The intended factor is exp(s(lambda(z)+lambda(z')-i*pi)), i.e. (zz')^s (-1)^{-s} in principal branches.

Index set: with mu = 0 and nu running over all nonzero integers, the axis terms (0,nu) and (0,-nu) are both included, while each line mu > 0 is counted once. The inversion maps both (0,nu) and (0,-nu) to (|nu|,0), and (mu,0) to (0,-mu). Literally, f(-1/z,-1/z') = e^{s(lambda(z)+lambda(z')-i pi)}[f(z,z') + zeta(2s)(e^{-s(lambda(z)+lambda(z'))} - e^{-i pi s})]. The stated functional equation is exact only for a genuine half-lattice, e.g. {mu>0, nu in Z} together with {mu=0, nu>0}. Equivalently, subtract the constant e^{-i pi s} zeta(2s) from Hilbert's f. A minor slip of the kind 'mu=0,nu=0 excluded' bookkeeping.

Overstatement: 'only when z, z' both have positive imaginary part does the series converge'. Absolute convergence (Re s > 1) holds whenever z and z' are non-real. The upper-half-plane condition is needed for the branch identities (A),(B) and for holomorphic consistency, not for convergence. Hilbert does not state the condition on s here (Re s > 1 suffices; p.121 had Re s > 2 for the one-variable series).

The displayed chain 'g(z+1,z''+1) = g(-1/z,-1/z'') = (?) g(z,z'')' conflates two relations. The translation has no factor, while the inversion carries exp(s(lambda(z)+lambda~(z'')-i pi)). The factor is missing or struck in the MS.

results.what: Two-variable Eisenstein-type series f(z,z') = sum (mu z+nu)^{-s}(mu z'-nu)^{-s} (careful branches) on H x H, invariant under (z,z')->(z+1,z'-1) and transforming with factor (zz')^s e^{-i pi s} under (z,z')->(-1/z,-1/z')
results.modern_name: Eisenstein series of complex weight (s,s) for SL2(Z) acting on H x H (twisted diagonal embedding); analogue of Hilbert-modular Eisenstein series sum N(mu z+nu)^{-s}
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert-modular Eisenstein series: Hecke (1912 Habilitation, 1920s); Hilbert's own Hilbert-modular ideas transmitted via Blumenthal (1903-04). Non-integral-weight series with branch control relate to Hurwitz/Lipschitz-era work.

results.what: Restriction z'' = conj(z) turns the holomorphic two-variable series into the zeta function of a positive definite binary quadratic form sum Q(mu,nu)^{-s}, with the phase exactly e^{-i pi s}
results.modern_name: Epstein zeta function / real-analytic (non-holomorphic) Eisenstein series E(z,s) viewed as restriction of a holomorphic function on H x H-bar (complexification of E(z,s))
results.usually_credited_to: The series: Dirichlet (class number formula, 1839), Kronecker (limit formula, 1863/1889), Weber (1891), Epstein (1903). Modular viewpoint: Maass (1949), Selberg. The complexification idea is folklore in later automorphic theory.

results.what: Term-by-term verification of the inversion law via exact logarithm-branch identities (A),(B), giving the multiplier with no e^{2 pi i k s} ambiguity
results.modern_name: Multiplier system / automorphy factor for complex weight

results.what: Translation invariance by reindexing nu -> nu - mu

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients are classical: Eisenstein-type series, the Dirichlet/Kronecker/Weber quadratic-form zeta function, and the SL2 action on binary forms. Hilbert's interest in such series in his early notebooks is plausible and fits his later Hilbert-modular programme. The notable unpublished detail is treating sum |mu z+nu|^{-2s} as the anti-diagonal restriction of a function holomorphic in two independent variables, with exact complex-weight functional equations, i.e. a two-variable 'Eisenstein series on H x H'. This anticipates in spirit both Hilbert-modular Eisenstein series (Hecke) and the modular view of real-analytic Eisenstein series (Maass). It is a sketch with a small index-set slip, not a developed theory.
